_README: Calibration inputs for the CSP simulator, with HONEST per-field provenance.
Container terminal statistics that ARE public (throughput, import/export vs
transshipment, size mix, full/empty) do NOT include a per-container weight-
CLASS frequency distribution -- the one input the CSP most needs. Verified
Gross Mass (VGM) is held by carriers/terminals and is not open data. So the
'weight_profile' below is an ASSUMPTION grounded in domain literature, NOT a
measured public statistic. Do not describe it as real terminal data.
To make it real, replace 'weight_profile' with measured VGM/TOS frequencies

utilization_provenance.basis: Storage-yard operational occupancy is typically ~0.60-0.75 in terminal-operations practice; 0.65 sits in that range and is consistent with the high-throughput regime of Korean ports (national container throughput reached 31.73M TEU in 2024; Busan 24.4M TEU).
utilization_provenance.note: Throughput/occupancy are public; they anchor utilization, not the weight distribution.

weight_profile_provenance.status: ASSUMPTION -- not measured, no public source exists
weight_profile_provenance.structure_is_real: Export containers ARE grouped into a few weight classes with heavier boxes loaded first, so a non-uniform, mid-heavy skew is realistic in shape (Kang et al. 2006; Cho et al. 2022; Lee & Cho 2025).
weight_profile_provenance.values_are_assumed: The specific per-class frequencies are a modelling choice; no open dataset publishes container weight-class frequencies (VGM is confidential).
weight_profile_provenance.how_to_replace: Set to measured per-voyage weight-class frequencies from a terminal TOS/VGM export (route B: H4Tech / KHT channel).

_paper_wording: Report results under this profile only as a robustness check under a non-uniform weight distribution, NOT as a real-terminal validation, until 'weight_profile' is replaced with measured values.
